name: Bleed valve and bleed line
function: A small manual valve on the header that bleeds trapped pressure from the manifold to a tank or pit after pumping stops and before any connection is broken.

tabs.overview: Bleed lines run to a tank away from the work area. Bleeding is done slowly; a manifold full of slurry can hold pressure behind settled sand.
tabs.engineering: Small-bore gate or needle valve rated with the manifold.
tabs.safety: Verify zero at the transducer after bleeding; trapped pressure behind packed sand is a known cause of injuries when unions are broken.
tabs.evidence: API 6A (S1) for pressure-containing parts and connections; public OEM pages (S2, S3, S5, S11, S12) for configurations; field and manufacturing practice (S9).

hazards.control: Pressure test before pumping; bleed down and verify zero before breaking any connection.
Restraints and whip checks on iron; exclusion zone around pressurized lines.
